actions.question: What mechanisms underpin the development of responsibility and accountability in autonomous agents?
actions.reason: Project active, requires structural hypothesis to progress without external search.
actions.title: Agency and Responsibility in AI

assumptions: Autonomous agents possess internal state representations.
Causal attribution models can be explicitly defined within agent architecture.
Accountability is emergent from the agent's ability to map actions to consequences in its local model.
definition.falsification: If agents with advanced causal modeling capabilities demonstrate no improvement in accountability metrics compared to baseline agents, the internal causal-map theory is falsified.
definition.statement: The attribution of responsibility in autonomous systems is a function of the agent's internal model of its own causal impact, rather than the complexity of its decision-making algorithm.
definition.uncertainty: The precise definition of 'responsibility' in an algorithmic context remains underspecified.

proposal.summary: Advancing the investigation into AI responsibility frameworks via hypothesis-driven inquiry while navigating search slot constraints.
proposal.title: Responsibility Formation and Agency Mapping
